features.title: Owned crate cfg_attr no_std policy in authenticated closed configuration
features.scope: Retains original crate-root cfg_attr predicate/payload AST and spans; evaluates feature/all/any/not/literal predicates only in the genuine same-source/edition/target no-explicit-cfg checker context. No source rewriting, unknown-active-attribute stripping, forged token, Cargo feature inference or project acceptance. Original-crate and authored native/reference obligations are UNRUN pending CI; no new qualification evidence is recorded.

features.title: Local nominal inherent associated functions and by-value methods
features.scope: Checked nongeneric/generic local record and enum impls; self/mut self, Self names, qualified calls, explicit full impl type arguments, declaration-checked non-Copy generic bodies, source-order one-time receiver evaluation and recursion via shared instance registry. Excludes reference receivers, autoderef/autoborrow, trait impls, coherence specialization, method-local generic parameters, arbitrary self types and reference/Drop runtime. Qualified only in host pcc0/self Linux x86-64, with actual unchanged-source native rustc1.91.1 differential; Darwin remains cross-emission only.

features.title: Actually checked readonly direct calls and shared receivers
features.scope: Readonly references and &self receivers to admitted places use actual same-input source/options-bound external checking before owned typed-pointer lowering. All original eight shared-reference programs retain their bytes and full-eight-byte native/reference outputs. The flag alone never authorizes any public reference-bearing input; the checked route bypasses incomplete owned loan/move admission while retaining nonborrow type, addressability and mutability checks. The old partial loan algorithm is only an explicitly nonlowering internal mechanism, not a public admission gate or borrow certification. Reference returns, aggregate reference storage, nested references, temporary lifetime extension, arbitrary traits and Drop remain outside scope. Linux x86-64 runtime qualification only; missing Darwin target core/std leaves reference cases explicitly unrun.
